_note: Real-user walkthrough notes reported by the reviewers themselves (October 2026). Informal walkthroughs, not a formal timed study; the two sessions were not identical. Feedback fields hold verbatim excerpts of the reviewers' own written feedback.

walkthroughs.session: Quick walkthrough: checked recommendations on the reconciliation and approval screens, including the spouse-account payment, an agent discrepancy and a held reminder
feedback: The recommendations generally matched the decisions I would have made myself.
What I liked most was that the system did not treat every mismatch as a customer problem.
I would not want a customer who had already paid to receive a late-payment message simply because the payment had not yet been reconciled.
The “Why?” evidence view gave me enough information to judge the recommendation rather than simply trusting the AI.

I do not have a reliable historical time study, so I would not claim an exact number of hours saved, but a 4-minute prioritized review is materially different from manually reconstructing each case across separate records.

walkthroughs.session: Review of the Morning Control Room, reconciliation cases, approval queue, held reminders and the liquidity view
feedback: Instead of showing an operations person every transaction and expecting them to find the problems, Alajo Control surfaced the cases that actually needed attention and explained why they were flagged.
The held-reminder feature was particularly useful because it reduces the risk of contacting customers incorrectly when there is evidence that they may already have paid.
The liquidity view was also useful because it connected individual reconciliation issues to the broader question of whether upcoming customer payouts were adequately covered.
That made the product feel more like an operations control system than simply a transaction dashboard.
